source.title: What Do EEG Foundation Models Capture from Human Brain Signals?
source.authors: Ling Tang; Qian Chen; Jilin Mei; Houshi Xu; Quanshi Zhang; Jing Shao; Na Zou; Xia Hu; Dongrui Liu

record.tranche_reason: Tests recurrence of interpretable, hand-crafted EEG features across foundation models in a new EEG setting, using feature probing and causal erasure rather than model-to-model representation-distance comparisons.
record.gate_note: The study tests whether established EEG features are encoded and causally used across models. It does not measure similarity between models' distances on shared inputs, cross-modal alignment, scale trends, or learned neuron/circuit recurrence.
record.test_reason: It asks whether the same interpretable features recur across three independently trained EEG foundation models (CSBrain, CBraMod, LaBraM). The features are a fixed catalogue of 63 hand-crafted EEG features, tested by linear probing and causal erasure on five tasks. This is a loose fit to V5: the features are human-defined input properties rather than learned neurons or SAE features, and the models are never compared directly.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that the three EEG foundation models encode (about 90%) and causally use (about 69%) most of the hand-crafted catalogue, with broadly shared, task-dependent usage. The used features recover 79.3% of each model's advantage over a random-feature baseline, with leftover unexplained performance on harder tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses layer-wise ridge probes and LEACE-style cross-covariance subspace erasure on a predefined EEG feature catalog, rather than comparing distances between independently trained models. Tests three EEG architectures on five EEG tasks.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported cross-model feature categories vary by task: universal candidates require unanimous model support on at least two tasks, while task-specific and model-specific categories capture more limited recurrence.
record.code_released: An anonymized version is included with supplementary material; a public repository is planned for the camera-ready version. No URL stated.
record.problems: Evidence is limited to three architectures, five EEG tasks, and a predefined hand-crafted feature catalog. The feature audit uses linear probes and a covariance-simplified eraser rather than the closed-form LEACE operator; it does not test learned neuron or circuit recurrence.

untested.parts: No sweep of model size or capability, and no comparison of representations between models.
No vision or language models and no paired data.
No comparison across random seeds or initializations.
No mapping, stitching or interchangeability test between models.
No recurrence of learned neurons, SAE features or circuits. Only a predefined human feature catalogue is tested, in three EEG models.
No comparison of similarity metrics, and no out-of-distribution inputs.
No test of shared data or objectives as the cause, and no plateau measured.

missing.what: Encoding rate across cells: 847 of 945 units (89.6%) encoded, and all 63 features encoded in at least one cell. Also 648 of 945 (68.6%) units are representation-causal.
Number of representation-causal features per model and task, showing cross-model divergence (e.g., Stress: CSBrain 6, CBraMod 47, LaBraM 29).
The same feature sits at different peak layers in the three architectures.

record.verdict_notes: V5 fit is loose. Decodability of input-derived features such as band power from any rich representation may be near-trivial, though the causal-erasure criterion is stronger. The universal-candidate count depends on the study's criterion: all three models, at least two tasks, FDR threshold and linear eraser. No versions other than V5 are tested.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, and no comparison of representation distances across independently trained models.
No paired images and captions or vision-language models.
No comparison across random initializations or analysis of shared subspaces versus individual units.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
Tests recurrence of catalogued hand-crafted EEG features across three architectures, not recurrence of neurons, SAE features, or circuits; the study covers only its three models and five tasks.
No comparison of representation-convergence measures, their settings, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain model-to-model representation alignment, or measure a convergence plateau.

tranche.reason: Tests recurrence of interpretable features in a new setting: three EEG foundation models across five clinical tasks.

source_check.notes: The audit uses released task-fine-tuned checkpoints with frozen backbones; its causal evidence concerns linear, target-correlated subspace erasure rather than matched neurons. The reported 79.3% closure is an average across 15 model–task cells.
